content.label: Examiner note - ionic language discipline
content.body: Say 'electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions' - that sentence is the mark. Never call an ionic compound a molecule: it is a giant lattice, which is exactly why its melting point is high (every ion must be pulled from the whole network, not from one partner). And in the solid it does not conduct - the ions are locked in place; molten or dissolved, they move and carry charge.
